note: Where the call to action goes, how long it holds and how it is worded, per platform and per format. `start_pct` is percent of runtime. A CTA states one next step; urgency only if it is true; no invented offers. Narrative: docs/research/launch-video-patterns.md#ctas.

grades.platform: the platform's own help or spec page

youtube.endscreen.rule: plan the last 20 s in the edit as low-information footage under the end screen elements; stagger the elements

ad.endcard.where: the last 2.0 s of a 15 s ad, the last 2.5 s of longer cuts
ad.endcard.rule: the end card holds >= 1.8 s after its motion settles; one verb; the brand cue already landed inside the action earlier

ad.direction.rule: a clear, simple next step in writing, graphics, audio or a story scene (ABCD 'Direction')

tiktok.close.rule: end with a strong CTA; brand early but subtle so it does not weaken the hook

meta.reels.rule: keep burned-in CTA text inside the safe zone (top 14%, bottom 35%, 6% each side); the ad's own CTA button sits in the bottom band, so do not burn one in there

soft.midroll.rule: a soft CTA (a send line, a 'link below') before the end card, for viewers who leave before the end

short.video.where: the end, for videos under 5 min
short.video.rule: under 5 min the CTA goes at the end; over 5 min, at the beginning as well
short.video.note_source: practitioner or study source named in the research doc

launch.film.rule: one CTA, not three; on a launch platform that bans vote requests, ask the viewer to try it, never to vote
launch.film.note_source: practitioner or study source named in the research doc

founder.ask.rule: the smallest possible ask: one URL or one instruction
founder.ask.note_source: practitioner or study source named in the research doc

trailer.datecard.where: after the title and the button, the last 2-4 s
trailer.datecard.rule: a specific date on a trailer, a vague one (a season) on a teaser
trailer.datecard.note_source: practitioner or study source named in the research doc

podcast.clip.rule: a soft pointer to the full episode; never cut the punchline to fit the ask
podcast.clip.note_source: practitioner or study source named in the research doc

loop.short.where: a small tag, not a card
loop.short.rule: on a looping Short, replace the end card with a small tag at 0.8 opacity outside the bottom 35% so the seam stays clean

rules: Say what happens next, in the viewer's words.
Urgency only if it is true.
No 'free', '100%' or 'guaranteed' unless literally true and approved.
Name an audience in the send line ('send this to ...'); never ask for a keyword comment.
examples: Try it on your next draft.
Start a plan in one click.
Send this to whoever runs your launches.
